title: Boreal forest fire regime shift
bottleneck: Boreal forests are shifting from a regime of stand-replacing fires every century to megafires that burn deeper into soils and peat, releasing carbon accumulated over millennia — but whether forests regenerate or convert to shrubland or grassland depends on fire severity, seed sources, and permafrost thaw in ways models capture poorly. The 2023-2024 Canadian fire seasons burned areas unprecedented in the satellite record, yet carbon accounting still treats such events as anomalies rather than the new baseline.
why_it_blocks: Boreal forests and peatlands are the largest terrestrial carbon store; a permanent shift to a high-fire regime would convert them from sink to source, adding warming no policy currently budgets for. Fire management built for the old regime is already overwhelmed.
current_state: Research is racing to map burn severity to regeneration outcomes, and Indigenous fire stewardship offers proven management models. But the climate-fire-vegetation feedback is intensifying faster than the science or the firefighting capacity.
